name: Make America Number 1

summary.text: Make America Number 1 is a super PAC that began in 2015 as Keep the Promise I, a pro-Ted Cruz committee funded almost entirely by Robert Mercer, and was renamed in June 2016 to focus on advertising against Hillary Clinton. It paid Cambridge Analytica several million dollars; the Campaign Legal Center filed FEC complaints (MUR 7147) alleging coordination with the Trump campaign through the shared vendor and through payments linked to Steve Bannon and Kellyanne Conway. Those are allegations; no FEC finding was located.

facts.claim: CNN reported on June 23, 2016 that the super PAC Keep the Promise I, funded almost entirely by $13.5 million from Robert Mercer, had been renamed Make America Number 1 and would focus primarily on advertising opposing Hillary Clinton rather than supporting Trump, and that it would be run by David Bossie, president of Citizens United.
facts.quote: funded almost entirely by $13.5 million from Republican megadonor Robert Mercer

sources.title: Yet another Donald Trump super PAC launches, this one with a link to Ted Cruz

facts.claim: The Campaign Legal Center's FEC complaint (MUR 7147) states that Make America Number 1 paid at least $4,633,876 to Cambridge Analytica, a firm whose board included Steve Bannon and Robert Mercer, and alleges that the Trump campaign began contracting with Cambridge Analytica at the request of the Mercer family, raising a common-vendor coordination problem. These are the complainant's allegations.
facts.quote: Make America Number 1 (also known as the "Defeat Crooked Hillary" super PAC) made unlawful and unreported expenditures in coordination with the campaign

sources.title: Campaign Legal Center supplemental complaint, MUR 7147 (Make America Number 1 / Cambridge Analytica)
New Evidence Suggests Mercer-Backed Super PAC Unlawfully Coordinated with Trump Campaign

facts.claim: The Campaign Legal Center alleged that the super PAC effectively paid Trump campaign CEO Steve Bannon through Glittering Steel and Cambridge Analytica, and that FEC records show payments to Kellyanne Conway's polling company and to Glittering Steel after Conway and Bannon joined the Trump campaign in August 2016. The CLC said David Bossie left the super PAC in September 2016 to become Trump's deputy campaign manager.
facts.quote: Make America Number 1 appeared to have paid compensation to Trump campaign CEO Stephen K. Bannon

New Evidence Suggests Mercer-Backed Super PAC Unlawfully Coordinated with Trump Campaign

facts.claim: NPR reported in March 2018 that a pro-Trump super PAC paid Cambridge Analytica $5.7 million, almost the same sum as the Trump campaign's $5.9 million, and noted that while a campaign and super PAC cannot coordinate their messages, they may hire the same vendor.

sources.title: Cambridge Analytica's Role In Trump's 2016 Campaign Raises Potential Legal Flags

facts.claim: On October 16, 2020 the Campaign Legal Center filed a supplemental complaint based on newly published internal Cambridge Analytica documents, alleging the firm ignored its own written firewall policy and that the super PAC and campaign shared a project calendar. Cambridge Analytica denied using the data in Trump's 2016 campaign.
facts.quote: On Oct. 16, 2020, CLC filed a supplemental complaint based on newly-published internal Cambridge Analytica documents

openQuestions: Mercer's total giving to the committee is reported variously as $11 million, $13.5 million and $15.5 million depending on the period; confirm from FEC receipts.
NPR refers to the pro-Trump super PAC that paid $5.7 million as 'Stop Crooked Hillary PAC'; confirm the FEC committee name.
Kellyanne Conway's role heading the committee from August 2015 and David Bossie's exact departure month were stated only by tertiary sources or the CLC; confirm from FEC statements of organization.
